title: Check your understanding: Git and Software Supply-Chain Integrity

questions.prompt: Which statement best describes the purpose of git and software supply-chain integrity?
options: Software supply-chain integrity depends on verifiable source, review, controlled credentials, build provenance and artifact verification. Git signatures help with part of this picture but do not prove that code is safe.
Git automatically backs up every file, including ignored and untracked files, to a remote.
The operation grants every contributor write access to the hosted repository.
questions.answer_key: Software supply-chain integrity depends on verifiable source, review, controlled credentials, build provenance and artifact verification. Git signatures help with part of this picture but do not prove that code is safe.
questions.explanation: Software supply-chain integrity depends on verifiable source, review, controlled credentials, build provenance and artifact verification. Git signatures help with part of this picture but do not prove that code is safe.

questions.prompt: Which command is the most direct starting point for this lesson’s example?
questions.explanation: Use `git verify-tag v1.0.0` as the first inspection/action in the example, and then verify the result with the companion checks in the lesson.

questions.prompt: Which is the safest general practice when working with git and software supply-chain integrity?
options: Inspect the repository state, verify the expected result, and protect valuable work before destructive or history-changing operations.
Run the most destructive option first; the reflog guarantees every file can always be recovered.
Assume the local command also changed the remote and satisfied all hosting-platform policies.
questions.answer_key: Inspect the repository state, verify the expected result, and protect valuable work before destructive or history-changing operations.
questions.explanation: Inspect the repository state, verify the expected result, and protect valuable work before destructive or history-changing operations.
